# sessionsnap

> Save and resume your coding-agent sessions in cmux and tmux.

sessionsnap saves named, versioned snapshots of cmux workspaces (or tmux sessions) and the coding-agent sessions in their tabs, and reopens only what is missing, with each agent tab resumed in its own folder with the flags it was started with. It is a single Rust binary with a CLI, a web UI in the cmux Dock (or the default browser from tmux), cmux palette commands and a Claude Code skill. Nothing runs in the background unless you add an automatic snapshot (`schedule add`).

It needs macOS with cmux 0.64 or newer, or tmux on macOS or Linux: sessionsnap uses the terminal it runs in (tmux first; outside both, the one running), and `--terminal cmux|tmux` picks one. cmux on Linux is a different app with a different command line, not supported yet.

Claude Code, Codex and Pi are fully supported and tested (their session histories are read; Pi's launch flags need `sessionsnap install-pi`). 14 more agents (Grok, OpenCode, omp, Campfire, Amp, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Rovo Dev, Hermes Agent, GitHub Copilot CLI, CodeBuddy, Factory Droid, Qoder CLI) are resumed with the command cmux documents for them, and are untested.

## For agents driving sessionsnap

- Always pass `--json` and read the result; never parse the text output.
- Restoring is two steps: `sessionsnap restore <name> --plan --json`, show the user the plan, then `sessionsnap apply <planId> --json` once they agree.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (code `usage` for a mistyped command), 2 terminal unreachable, 3 nothing to do, 4 refused (code `needs-confirmation`: ask the user, never add `--yes` on your own), 5 unknown cmux state or snapshot format, 6 plan stale, 7 not found. Output is one compact JSON line when stdout is not a terminal; `sessions` and `recent` take `--limit`; `list --cwd <dir>` keeps the snapshots with something in that folder, and its rows name their workspaces, folders and agents; `restore` with no name plans the most recently saved snapshot.
- Never pass `--yes` to `delete`, `prune`, `install-cmux` or `uninstall` unless the user asked for that exact action. Never start an automatic snapshot (`schedule add`) unless asked.

## Commands

`save`, `list`, `open`, `show`, `history`, `diff`, `prune`, `delete`, `rename`, `export`, `import`, `schedule`, `ws`, `tab`, `edit`, `restore`, `apply`, `sessions`, `recent`, `agents`, `ui`, `install-cmux`, `install-skill`, `install-pi`, `completions`, `man`, `update`, `uninstall`. Every command has `--help`.

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://sessionsnap.pawanpaudel.com.np/install.sh | sh
```
